key_insight: HIPE-2026 establishes a standardized evaluation for extracting person–place relations from noisy, multilingual historical texts, balancing accuracy and runtime efficiency to reflect real-world digital-humanities needs.
problem_solved: Lack of a benchmark and shared task for reliably identifying person–place associations (two relation types: at / isAt) across OCR-noisy, multilingual and diachronic historical sources, with an emphasis on both correctness and computational efficiency.
method: Organize a CLEF evaluation lab with curated multilingual, diachronic corpora annotated for two relation types (at vs isAt) to reflect presence vs contemporaneous location.
Define clear annotation guidelines and evaluation metrics that measure both extraction accuracy (precision/recall/F1) and runtime/efficiency for practical deployments.
Provide baseline systems, submission protocols and multilingual test sets to foster comparable, reproducible benchmarking of robust relation-extraction models.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners and digital-humanities researchers a reproducible benchmark to develop and compare robust, efficient relation-extraction systems for noisy historical text, accelerating practical tools for historical data exploration and analysis.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: OCR → tokenization → NER → relation classifier (highlighting where noise affects performance)
Map + timeline visualization: person nodes linked to places with time-slider to illustrate at vs isAt distinctions
Scatter plot (accuracy vs latency): comparing submitted systems to emphasize the accuracy-efficiency trade-off
Coverage heatmap: languages × time periods showing dataset distribution and challenge density
paper_title: CLEF HIPE-2026: Evaluating Accurate and Efficient Person-Place Relation Extraction from Multilingual Historical Texts
paper_authors: Juri Opitz, Corina Raclé, Emanuela Boros, Andrianos Michail, Matteo Romanello
